adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 253-255 in the diff for GoogleCalendarService.ts updateEvent method: `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;` - When externalCalendarId is falsy (absent), the code falls back to searching destinationCalendar for a calendar where `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`. But since externalCalendarId is falsy at this point, this search will never find a match (comparing against undefined/null), so selectedCalendar will be undefined. This causes the calendar.events.update to use undefined as calendarId, which likely defaults to 'primary'. This is a logical bug - the fallback condition searches for the very value that was already determined to be absent.
